span.label: pseudospin —renamed-across-fields→ real spin
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER STATES THE IMPORT AND ITS GROUND IN ONE SENTENCE: similar to the spin index (up and down) IN QED and, THEREFORE, is referred to as pseudospin. The naming is argued for, not assumed - the analogy is the stated reason for the word.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: pseudospin —distinct-from→ real spin
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — AND THE PAPER IMMEDIATELY FENCES THE BORROWED WORD OFF FROM THE ONE IT CAME FROM: the symbol Quotation withheld. Borrowing the name and denying the identity, in the same paragraph.

span.label: chirality —renamed-across-fields→ Dirac equation
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — BY ANALOGY WITH QED, one can also introduce a quantity called chirality - the second term imported by declared analogy rather than by derivation. | SPAN WIDENED because `chirality` occurs in the original sentence only as `chirality6` - the reference marker is glued to the word, so the endpoint was not attested AS A WORD. The wider span reaches two bare uses. substring-is-not-a-word, enforced by the gate rather than by me.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Fermi velocity —operationalised-as→ Dirac equation
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — The borrowed equation is made to fit by SUBSTITUTING ONE CONSTANT: the Fermi velocity plays the role of the speed of light. That substitution carries the whole analogy, and the paper quantifies its size elsewhere as c/vF of about 300.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: zero-gap semiconductor —same-as→ zero-overlap semimetals
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — An explicit in-text renaming: CAN ALSO BE REFERRED TO AS. Two vocabularies, one class, and the paper declines to choose between them.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Dirac equation —contrasted-with→ Schrödinger equation
span.note: differs in: which equation the material's carriers are naturally described by - the paper makes graphene the exception to the rule it states in the same sentence · strength of the relation: 0.9

span.label: massive Dirac fermions —contrasted-with→ massless Dirac fermions
span.note: differs in: rest mass - and the paper records that the borrowed framework CANNOT HOLD the combination: massive chiral particles would be an oxymoron in relativistic quantum theory · strength of the relation: 0.9
